html:
Guinea left the CFA franc zone in March 1960 and issued its own Guinean franc, the first former French colony in Africa to do so.

It was part of Sekou Toure's break with France after the 1958 vote. The new money could not be exchanged freely, prices were fixed and trade was run by the state, and smuggling to neighbours grew. The currency was replaced by the syli in 1972 and the franc came back in 1986 after the change of regime. Its weak record is often cited in debates on whether other states should leave the CFA franc. Guinea's main export earner stayed bauxite.
sum: Guinea left the CFA franc zone in March 1960 and issued its own Guinean franc, the first former French colony in Africa to do so.
